hints.title: Sentence Suffix Reconstitution Obstacle
hints.text: Partitioning string s into space-separated dictionary words can produce multiple valid combinations. How can breaking off valid dictionary prefixes and solving suffixes avoid recomputing overlapping sub-problems?

hints.title: Suffix Sentence Subproblem Invariant
hints.text: The valid sentences that can be formed from suffix s[i:] depend only on dictionary words matching s[i:j] combined with sentences formed from s[j:].

hints.title: Recursive Prefix Partitioning Procedure
hints.text: Convert the dictionary into a fast lookup collection. Recursively find all valid sentence partitions for suffix s[start:]. For every prefix of the suffix matching a dictionary word, recursively obtain valid sentence suffixes for the remaining string and prepend the matching word. Cache suffix results to prevent redundant branch work. Return the completed sentences.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of input string s
complexity.notes: In the worst case, every substring partition is valid, resulting in exponential output size.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Pure recursive exploration without caching identical suffixes repeats redundant sub-trees.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Caching computed sentences for each suffix index prevents redundant recursive subproblem traversals.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Combining prefix lookup with cached suffix recursion to assemble all valid sentence configurations.
